outcome: Stimulation of inflammatory process in premature infants
cohort: The study included two groups of mothers-in-partum: 109 with a burdened medical history and 31 in a control group with healthy children.
finding: Mothers with a burdened medical history showed a higher prevalence of chronic fetoplacental insufficiency, preeclampsia, and C-sections, and specific maternal IgG levels for infections like Toxoplasma, CMV, and HSV were correlated with altered immune markers and inflammatory processes in their infants, particularly in premature infants.
mod_finding: Deliveries by Cesarean section were significantly more frequent among mothers with a burdened medical history compared to the control group (55.03% vs. 45.21%, p<0.01).
gest_age: N/A (premature infants mentioned but no specific gestational age)
